projectDescription: A new general-purpose 3D creation environment where AI agents create, inspect, modify, validate and revise scenes through a typed modeling API, and humans direct and directly edit everything.

context.userWorkflow: Stated 2026-11-03 at Decision 9: user drives modeling from VS Code / Claude Code; the website is a live view (watch, inspect, review), not the primary input surface.

decisions.title: Where the app runs
decisions.chosenTitle: Headless core + browser first (Electron later)

options.A: Headless core + browser first (Electron later)

decisions.caseAgainst: General-purpose production work is desktop-class (multi-GB scenes, native FBX/USD SDKs, real folders); browser limits (4GB WASM, Chromium-only folder access) may bake in; if an installer is needed within ~3 months, Electron from day one avoids a migration.
assumptions: Prototype ~6 weeks, scenes well under 4GB
Chromium acceptable for real file workflow
Engine package enforced DOM-free from commit one
tripwires: Need native SDKs (FBX, USD C++) or scenes approach 2-3GB -> wrap in Electron

decisions.title: Scene source of truth & change model
decisions.chosenTitle: Records + branching change log

options.A: Simple store + undo stack
options.B: Records + branching change log (patch transactions, content-addressed mesh blobs)

decisions.caseAgainst: Building a mini version-control system before proposals are proven; event-sourcing replay/migration tax; Loro gives fork/checkout/merge for free; Option A suffices for weeks 1-2.
assumptions: Edits flow through one validated typed-tool pipeline
Proposals/variants are a core differentiator
Meshes stored by content hash; snapshots every N commits
tripwires: Need simultaneous same-object multi-agent edits with auto-merge -> put Loro under the same record API

decisions.title: Construction model
decisions.chosenTitle: Typed op graph + code view

options.A: Modifier stack
options.D: Typed op graph + code view (named params, named anchors)

decisions.caseAgainst: Designing a language + editor is where solo projects die; benchmark geometric correctness ~0.35 regardless of format; much general-purpose content (characters, sculpts) isn't parametric, so a modifier stack might ship faster.
assumptions: Start with 15-25 ops, grow from benchmark failures
editableMesh escape-hatch op
Named anchors/datums, never face indices
Node view can be layered later
tripwires: If >40% of benchmark objects need raw mesh escapes, add a modifier-stack layer for mesh objects

decisions.title: Geometry kernel strategy
decisions.chosenTitle: Kernel interface, three engines (staged)

options.A: Manifold only
options.C: Kernel interface: Manifold + TS half-edge EditMesh + OpenSubdiv, OCCT lazy later

decisions.caseAgainst: Three kernels = three failure modes and buggy seams; mesh->B-rep is not recoverable; hand-written half-edge is subtle; Manifold-only for months proves the AI loop first.
assumptions: Weeks 1-3 Manifold only behind the interface
Explicit conversion ops with validity checks
All kernels in a Worker (browser) / in-process (Node)
tripwires: Manifold boolean artifacts in >5% of benchmark runs -> mesh-repair pass or OCCT booleans for those ops

decisions.title: How AI changes are reviewed

options.A: Ghost overlay
options.D: Change-by-change review (semantic change list, per-change Keep/Undo, viewport highlight, before/after flip)

decisions.title: Shape of the game toolset
decisions.chosenTitle: Asset forge + a real engine

options.A: One studio grows into a game maker (own browser runtime)
options.B: Family of studios on a shared core + own web runtime

assumptions: Goal is making games, not selling an engine
Studio's edge is checked, reviewable asset making
Target engine drivable headless from CLI
Hand-off owned by a checked export contract with round-trip tests
tripwires: Round-trip export tests fail repeatedly for skinned characters -> reconsider B for characters
You find yourself wanting to sell the engine -> revisit D

decisions.title: Target art style
decisions.chosenTitle: Low-poly + baked procedural materials

options.A: Low-poly, palette + material presets (PBR values travel in glTF)
options.E: Low-poly + procedural materials auto-baked to textures on export (auto-UV)

decisions.caseAgainst: Crowded look; and with A alone the studio’s procedural grain/glaze won’t show in-game until the bake (E) exists. Pick E now if the game must match the studio from day one.
assumptions: Solo/tiny team, Claude does most asset work
Palette + one shading model gives a recognizable look
Game-pipeline default, not a limit on the studio's prop materials
tripwires: Playtesters call the look generic -> add toon/outline shader and art-direct palette before considering B
Characters feel lifeless -> revisit for characters only

history.change: User asked whether in-progress materials work was considered; added material presets to A, added option E (baked procedural materials), recommendation A→E path, confidence strong→lean.

decisions.reasoning: User picked E (game should match the studio’s materials) over the lean recommendation A→E path.

decisions.title: Game targets: Godot for games, three.js for the web
decisions.chosenTitle: Two targets (Godot + three.js), one asset contract

options.D: Two targets + a portable game/level format compiled to each

assumptions: Projects are usually one target, rarely both
Web app = real site with UI + 3D view
Assets, baked materials, humanoid skeletons travel as glTF; Godot import script keeps studio-owned materials
D can be added later
tripwires: Same game wanted on both targets 2+ times -> add portable level format (D)
Shader/physics duplication eats more time than assets save -> narrow to one target per year

decisions.title: How characters get their shape
decisions.chosenTitle: Parametric character kits

options.B: Sculpt mode in the studio (SDF blends + brush)
options.D: Hand off to Blender via Blender MCP

assumptions: Low-poly characters
Animation reliability > one-off variety
Standard humanoid bone names, T-pose
Import used as reference to fit kit params
Blender as escape hatch
tripwires: Users/you reject characters as samey after 10+ made -> add C-shaped parts or hybrid
Need a body type the kit can't cover 3+ times -> build template or use D

Before v1 done: one real-newcomer round
decisions.chosenTitle: Question-led playtests, typed notes by default
decisions.reasoning: User: Option A, but don't force talking out loud and local transcription; let me just type my thoughts after playing.

decisions.title: First milestone for the game skills

options.A: Build skills alongside weeks 9-14; week 15 your own idea to great v1
options.C: Before Pocket Raleigh, proof week 12, Pocket Raleigh slips
options.D: Make Pocket Raleigh the first game through the skills

decisions.caseAgainst: Two builds at once; build skill chases landing modules; D more elegant if no idea ready.
tripwires: Build skill breaks twice from module change -> pause until module week ends
No idea by week 14 -> D
decisions.chosenTitle: Build alongside weeks 9–14, then take your idea to v1

decisions.title: The path from model to print

options.A: /studio print: checks -> Bambu Studio CLI builds A1 mini project (merged presets) -> opens in Bambu Studio -> you press Print; falls back to D
options.B: Headless slice, send via Bambu Connect
options.C: Straight to printer in LAN developer mode

decisions.caseAgainst: Bambu CLI has Apple Silicon crash bug; updates could break it; D has zero moving parts.
tripwires: CLI breaks twice after updates -> D default
decisions.chosenTitle: /studio print opens a ready project in Bambu Studio

decisions.title: Print-ready checks and fixes

options.A: Print profile (A1 mini, 0.4, PLA): live checks + fixes as proposals

decisions.caseAgainst: Overkill for occasional prints; duplicates slicer orient/supports; pre-slice overhang estimates rough.
tripwires: Overhang estimate often off vs slicer -> hint only
decisions.chosenTitle: A print profile: live checks, fixes you keep or undo

decisions.title: Colour without an AMS

options.A: One colour default + filament-change pause at a layer when colours split by height + one plate per colour for separate parts
options.C: Always split by colour into parts

decisions.caseAgainst: B may be all you use; height swaps need you present; AMS later changes by-part.
tripwires: Buy AMS lite -> one plate, filament per part
decisions.chosenTitle: One colour, always

decisions.title: Modelling helpers for print

options.A: Five helpers: fit (named gaps), fit-test coupon, text, hole, split with pegs

decisions.caseAgainst: May outrun occasional decorative prints; calibration drifts with filament.
tripwires: Ask for thread/gear/hinge twice -> add that helper
decisions.chosenTitle: Five everyday helpers, tuned to your printer

decisions.title: How the studio makes characters that don't look alike

options.A: Skeleton first (body plans: chibi, lanky, stocky, beaked biped; quadruped later) -> blob body on bones -> face from feature parts -> hair/outfit parts -> style family; cast outline check

decisions.caseAgainst: Biggest build; each body plan needs walk tuning; blob bodies can look soft; B gives variety faster for people-games.
tripwires: 3 new characters read as cousins -> style families before more skeletons
decisions.chosenTitle: Skeleton first, then any body, face and outfit

decisions.title: Rigging and motion for any shape the studio makes

options.A: Motion computed from each body's proportions (stride/cadence from leg length, IK foot planting, style settings), gestures on standard bone names, body-relative checks
options.C: Retarget human motions to every body

decisions.caseAgainst: Computed walks look bland; generalising is real work; hand-tuned may look better for 3-4 favourites.
tripwires: Plan looks generic after style pass -> hand-tuned walk override
decisions.chosenTitle: Motion built from each body's proportions

decisions.title: Faces and speech beyond the template face

options.A: Face parts carry their own 15 speech shapes + expressions (human mouth, cartoon mouth, beak, muzzle, grille); same names so lip sync/checks unchanged
options.B: Landmark transfer onto any finished face

decisions.caseAgainst: Only for studio-part faces; each mouth style is a mini project; parts may look stuck on.
tripwires: Part looks stuck on -> blend step
decisions.chosenTitle: Face parts that carry their own speech shapes

decisions.title: Outside characters as a side door

options.A: Rigged glTF/VRM import, auto bone map, own retargeter, faces from their shapes (ARKit > VRM vowels > jaw > eyes), VRM licence check, report; unrigged = props

decisions.caseAgainst: Rarely used if studio makes characters; retargeting fiddly; C covers stand-ins cheaply.
tripwires: Import unrigged models repeatedly -> add skeleton-adder
decisions.chosenTitle: Rigged models come in, with a report of what works

decisions.title: When to build it

options.A: Right after week 8 (weeks 9-11), Pocket Raleigh 12-17, your game week 18
options.B: Parallel third build in weeks 9-11, dates hold
options.D: Quick variety pass week 9, full system later

decisions.caseAgainst: Pocket Raleigh and game slip 3 weeks; B keeps dates. Tiebreaker: dates over simplicity -> B.
tripwires: Week 9 plans still cousins -> style families before motion
decisions.chosenTitle: Right after week 8, before Pocket Raleigh

decisions.title: How any shape gets a skeleton

options.A: Rig parts with procedural motion: legs xN, chains, wings, fins/body wave, wheels/tracks, hinges/sliders, springs, shader sway; body plans become combos; baked clips + live runtime
options.C: Fit skeleton to any finished shape

decisions.caseAgainst: Spore took weeks to learn what generalises; procedural looks generic; big build; Godot IK new and buggy; B looks better for few creatures.
tripwires: Part looks generic after style -> hand overrides
Godot IK misbehaves -> bake clips
decisions.chosenTitle: Rig parts that know how to move

decisions.title: How one-off motions get made from words

options.A: Claude writes key moments as part goals (end-effectors, lean, hinge angles, timing); studio solves with IK, easing, spring follow-through; checks; notes edit it; optional webcam (MediaPipe) start for human actions

decisions.caseAgainst: LLM key-posing mechanical for subtle human acting; several rounds of notes; research recent and human-focused.
tripwires: Safe any-skeleton model runs on Mac -> draft generator
Common human actions take 3+ rounds -> small CC0 clip library
decisions.chosenTitle: Claude directs key poses, the studio solves the rest

decisions.title: Checking any motion is believable

options.A: Each rig part declares contacts/limits/form; universal checks (penetration, balance for legged, pops, loops, idle end); failures on a timeline; clip + key-moment stills review

decisions.caseAgainst: General checks can pass wrong-looking motion (the crouch needed a specific check); no standard thresholds; cannot judge charm.
tripwires: You spot a problem checks passed -> add rule to that part
decisions.chosenTitle: Universal checks from the parts, plus a timeline to review

decisions.title: When to build it

options.A: Core parts + checks weeks 13-14 (legs, chains, wheels, hinges, springs, sway), Pocket Raleigh 15-20, wings/fins/one-off actions alongside, game week 21
options.C: In parallel, no delay, some rework

decisions.caseAgainst: Up to three builds; plan slipped twice already; C keeps dates. Tiebreaker: game sooner -> C.
tripwires: Framework not done by end wk 14 -> start Pocket Raleigh anyway
decisions.chosenTitle: Core parts first, the rest alongside Pocket Raleigh

decisions.title: How effects are made

options.A: Studio-owned effect description (shape effects first + particles), compiled to Godot .tres (+CPU fallback) and three.quarks JSON; look-lab colours; motion-event triggers; flipbooks only for smoke/explosions

decisions.caseAgainst: Two compilers; quarks schema undocumented; Godot web GPU particle support unsettled; Effekseer solves parity if plugin builds.
tripwires: Compilers drift visibly -> try Effekseer for that type
decisions.chosenTitle: Effects as studio assets, compiled to both engines

decisions.title: Checking and reviewing effects

options.A: Per-effect checks vs game profile (overdraw estimate, peak particles, fallback, look colours), Godot vs web frame diff, auto warm-up; side-by-side in-scene review

decisions.caseAgainst: Overdraw is an estimate; Mac-only proof; parity diffs may nag; desktop-first may only need clips.
tripwires: Parity flags >1 harmless diff per effect -> loosen per type
decisions.chosenTitle: Checks for cost and parity, side-by-side review

decisions.title: How 2D and UI art is made

options.A: UI kit generated from look-lab tokens: panels, buttons, bars, slots, tooltip, dialogue box -> Godot Theme + web CSS overlay; Claude-drawn SVG icons in a house style, rendered and scored, CC0 fallback; OFL fonts; checks for contrast, overflow, tap size, safe area
options.C: Claude writes UI styles per engine, no tool

decisions.caseAgainst: AI SVG icons weak beyond simple styles; small compiler for two outputs; B suffices for little UI.
tripwires: Icons inconsistent after scoring -> CC0 pack recoloured
decisions.chosenTitle: A UI kit generated from the look, for both engines

decisions.title: When to build it, and a first small game

options.A: Tiny real game now (wk 13-14, alongside rig-part framework), effects + UI kit wk 15-16 shaped by it, v1.1 shared wk 16, then Pocket Raleigh etc; no new tool modules until shared
options.B: Effects/UI after Pocket Raleigh, no small game (first game wk 23)
options.C: Effects/UI before Pocket Raleigh, no small game
options.D: Stop tools, make a game until it ships

decisions.caseAgainst: Tiny game predates game skills (ad hoc); two builds again; Pocket Raleigh moves a third time; B keeps plan steady.
tripwires: Not playable by end wk 14 -> cut scope
Freeze: no new tool modules until shared
decisions.chosenTitle: A tiny game now, effects and UI next, then a tool freeze

decisions.title: Which systems join the live view first

options.A: Everything that moves, on one timeline: motion, actions, voice, cutscenes, effects, sound
options.B: Pulled by your game: only the systems its spec uses
options.C: Places first: towns and town life
options.D: Plug-in frame first, then all nine systems

decisions.caseAgainst: Builds ahead of a real game (D59 lesson); B finds out for free if the game is a town builder or puzzle game.
assumptions: The live view stays the one shared place; separate players retire
Later systems plug in the same way
tripwires: Game spec uses none of the first group -> switch to B
First group > ~2 weeks -> ship what works, start the game
decisions.chosenTitle: Everything that moves, on one timeline (then the rest, all before your game)
decisions.reasoning: User picked B over the lean A: no view work ahead of the game; systems join in the order the game reaches them.

history.why: D65 = D (build all before the game) contradicted B; user switched 60 to A so everything that moves goes first, then the rest, all before the game.

decisions.title: How pointing at a moment works

options.A: Thing + its own clock + whole ticks (24000/s), anchored to named moments, version-stamped, stale not moved
options.C: Frame numbers at one project rate
options.D: Spot on a rendered picture at a timecode

decisions.caseAgainst: Most machinery before payoff; with D60=B maybe one system for a while, seconds would do.
tripwires: >1 in 10 notes go stale after ordinary edits -> anchor to named moments more often
decisions.chosenTitle: The thing, its own clock, whole-number ticks

decisions.title: What counts as a reviewable step outside modelling

options.A: One word note's worth = one step on the shared history; recipes stored, renders are caches; keep/undo with seen before/after; show-me-three on request, distinct, per section, losers discarded
options.B: Whole versions compared side by side
options.C: Every tiny edit is a step

decisions.caseAgainst: Each system must name its steps; renders re-made on demand; B is far less work for one game with few changes in flight.
tripwires: >9 in 10 steps kept without opening -> group steps
decisions.chosenTitle: One note's worth of change is one step, three on request

decisions.title: The notes inbox and the taste file

options.A: One notes inbox per project (D61 addresses, open/on it/done/stale) + taste.md in plain words with evidence, editable, read before proposals; studio-wide + per-game; private by default
options.B: Inbox; taste stays in Claude's memory

decisions.caseAgainst: A taste file can be confidently wrong and steer proposals until noticed; D self-updates, B adds nothing.
tripwires: Taste file > ~30 rules -> prune
decisions.chosenTitle: One inbox per project, plus a taste file in plain words

decisions.title: "Only you can judge" checklists

options.A: Two-part card per proposal: 'I checked' + 'Your call' (<=3 skippable taps; skipped wait in inbox; answers feed taste)
options.B: Saved up for milestone review sessions
options.C: Summaries say what Claude couldn't check; user chooses

decisions.caseAgainst: Many small asks add up and invite rubber-stamping; B respects attention more.
tripwires: User skips > half the asks for a week -> fold into milestone sessions (B)
decisions.chosenTitle: A short "your call" card on each proposal

decisions.title: Build order around your game

options.A: Thin shared core first (~1 week, proven on models), then your game pulls systems in
options.B: Game now, every piece built inside it
options.C: Game first with today's tools + pain log, then core from the pain
options.D: Everything first, then the game (conflicts with D60)

decisions.caseAgainst: C repeats the Fire's Dying method that worked; A delays the game a week for plumbing untested by a second system.
tripwires: Core not usable within ~7 working days -> start the game anyway (C)
decisions.chosenTitle: Build it all first, then your game
decisions.reasoning: User chose to build the whole working-together layer before their own game.
